newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana clinics sue over new abortion law.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana clinics sue over new abortion law.

text.p: A group of women's health care providers filed suit in U.S. District Court Monday to block enforcement of a new state law charging doctors with a felony if they perform so-called "partial-birth abortions."

The suit, filed just hours after Gov. Mike Foster signed the new proposal into law, claimed the law's definition of "partial-birth abortions" is so vague that it could be applied to commonly accepted methods of abortion such as the dilation and evacuation method, as well as the more controversial dialation and extraction method.

The legal challenge was filed by Causeway Medical Suite, Bossier City Medical Suite, Hope Medical Group for Women, Delta Women's Clinic, Women's Health Clinic, James DeGuerce, M.D., and A. James Whitmore III, M.D.
William Rittenberg, one of several plaintiff's attorneys, said, "This abortion ban epitomises the worst of Louisiana -- it is bad policy and bad medicine."

The suit also claims the law prevents physicians from exercising their best medical judgment for their patients and in some cases the threat of prosecution could force doctors to use methods that may impose unnecessary health risks on women.
The suit seeks an immediate restraining order. No ruling was issued Monday.
